title: Jacob (with a colleague): real-to-sim data-synthesis pipelines with VLMs - is per-scene physical calibration by a VLM-driven robot adopted and worth it versus a material-prior database plus randomization; sim-to-sim as the training ground for a VLM synthesizer; how to evaluate a data synthesizer (transfer score) and a batch of synthetic data; whether training an open VLM is justified
abstract: Seven questions, answered with 73 fetched abstracts, 8 pages and a 75-paper agent x real2sim2real list in data/threads/PROGRAM-L5-simulators.md Part V: calibration is a minority practice (1 of 27 agent papers revises physical parameters on a real robot; industry assigns friction by assumption); the evidence splits by task sensitivity (2606.22062, Phys2Real, ForceTwin versus cousins, co-training, MetaGenSim, InternData-A1); twins are for evaluation and replay, cousins for training; sim-to-sim is valid cross-engine; the transfer score is a two-sample test on binary outcomes with a 10-point standard error at n = 50, with fixes in print (SureSim, sequential tests, paired evaluation); the data-value metric exists (influence functions: CUPID, QoQ, ATHENA, TUCO for sim demos); training the VLM is occupied (3D-Generalist, PhysX-Anything, SpatialLM) and the harness outlives the weights (Agentic Real2Sim). One claim captured: CL-W45-J01 (the per-parameter value of calibration under a material prior, computable in simulation; concept-level kill search survived).
